account.description: The Account that the Application belongs to.

environment.description: The Environment that the Application belongs to.

propeller.description: The Application's Propeller. If no Propeller is provided, Propel will set the Propeller to `P1_X_SMALL`. The valid values are `P1_X_SMALL`, `P1_SMALL`, `P1_MEDIUM`, `P1_LARGE` and `P1_X_LARGE`

scopes.description: The Application's API authorization scopes. If specified, at least one scope must be provided; otherwise, all scopes will be granted to the Application by default.

block.description: Provides a Propel Application resource.

access_control_enabled.description: Whether the Data Pool has access control enabled or not. If the Data Pool has access control enabled, Applications must be assigned Data Pool Access Policies in order to query the Data Pool and its Metrics.

account.description: The Account that the Data Pool belongs to.

data_source.description: The Data Source that the Data Pool belongs to.

environment.description: The Environment that the Data Pool belongs to.

table.description: The name of the Data Pool's table.

tenant_id.description: The tenant ID for restricting access between customers.

unique_id.description: The Data Pool's unique ID column. Propel uses the primary timestamp and a unique ID to compose a primary key for determining whether records should be inserted, deleted, or updated within the Data Pool. Only for Snowflake Data Pools.

clickhouse_type.description: The ClickHouse type to use when `type` is set to `CLICKHOUSE`.

nullable.description: Whether the column's type is nullable or not.

block.description: The list of columns, their types and nullability.

last_synced_at.description: The date and time of the most recent Sync in UTC.

status.description: Indicates whether syncing is enabled or disabled.

block.description: The Data Pool's syncing settings.

order_by.description: The ORDER BY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

partition_by.description: The PARTITION BY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

primary_key.description: The PRIMARY KEY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

columns.description: The columns argument for the SummingMergeTree table engine.

ver.description: The `ver` parameter to the ReplacingMergeTree table engine.

block.description: The ClickHouse table engine for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

Override the Data Pool's table settings. These describe how the Data Pool's table is created in ClickHouse, and a default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if any. You can override these defaults in order to specify a custom table engine, custom ORDER BY, etc.
Provides a Propel Data Pool resource. This can be used to create and manage Propel Data Pools.

account.description: The Account to which the Data Pool Access Policy belongs.

applications.description: The list of applications to which the Access Policy is assigned.

columns.description: The list of columns that the Access Policy makes available for querying. Set "*" to allow all columns.

data_pool.description: The Data Pool to which this Access Policy belongs.

description.description: The Data Pool Access Policy's description.

environment.description: The Environment to which the Data Pool Access Policy belongs.

unique_name.description: The Data Pool Access Policy's name.

and.description: Additional filters to AND with this one. AND takes precedence over OR. It is defined as a JSON string value.

column.description: The name of the column to filter on.

operator.description: The operation to perform when comparing the column and filter values.

or.description: Additional filters to OR with this one. AND takes precedence over OR. It is defined as a JSON string value.

value.description: The value to compare the column to.

block.description: Row-level filters that the Access Policy applies before executing queries. Not setting any row filters means all rows can be queried.

account.description: The Account that the Data Source belongs to.

created_at.description: The date and time of when the Data Source was created.

created_by.description: The user who created the Data Source.

environment.description: The Environment that the Data Source belongs to

modified_at.description: The date and time of when the Data Source was modified.

modified_by.description: The user who modified the Data Source.

type.description: The Data Source's type. Depending on this, you will need to specify one of `snowflake_connection_settings`, `s3_connection_settings`, `http_connection_settings`, `webhook_connection_settings`, `kafka_connection_settings` or `clickhouse_connection_settings`. The valid values are `SNOWFLAKE`, `S3`, `HTTP`, `WEBHOOK`, `KAFKA` and `CLICKHOUSE`

password.description: The password for the provided user.

readonly.description: Whether the user has readonly permissions or not for querying ClickHouse.

url.description: The URL where the ClickHouse host is listening to HTTP[S] connections.

user.description: The user for authenticating against the ClickHouse host.

password.description: Password for HTTP Basic authentication that must be included in the Authorization header when uploading new data.

username.description: Username for HTTP Basic authentication that must be included in the Authorization header when uploading new data.

block.description: The HTTP basic authentication settings. If this parameter is not provided, anyone with the URL will be able to send events. While it's OK to test without HTTP Basic authentication, we recommend enabling it.

auth.description: The type of authentication to use. Can be SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512, PLAIN or NONE.

bootstrap_servers.description: The bootstrap server(s) to connect to.

password.description: The password for the provided user.

tls.description: Whether the the connection to the Kafka servers is encrypted or not.

user.description: The user for authenticating against the Kafka servers.

aws_access_key_id.description: The AWS access key ID for an IAM user with sufficient access to the S3 bucket.

aws_secret_access_key.description: The AWS secret access key for an IAM user with sufficient access to the S3 bucket.

bucket.description: The name of the S3 bucket.

account.description: The Snowflake account. Only include the part before the "snowflakecomputing.com" part of your Snowflake URL (make sure you are in classic console, not Snowsight). For AWS-based accounts, this looks like "znXXXXX.us-east-2.aws". For Google Cloud-based accounts, this looks like "ffXXXXX.us-central1.gcp".

role.description: The Snowflake role. It should be "PROPELLER" if you used the default name in the setup script.

username.description: The Snowflake username. It should be "PROPEL" if you used the default name in the setup script.

warehouse.description: The Snowflake warehouse name. It should be "PROPELLING" if you used the default name in the setup script.

block.description: Snowflake connection settings. Specify these for Snowflake Data Sources.

path.description: The path to the table's files in S3.

nullable.description: Whether the column's type is nullable or not.

webhook_url.description: The Webhook URL for posting JSON events.

username.description: Username for HTTP Basic authentication that must be included in the Authorization header when uploading new data.

nullable.description: Whether the column's type is nullable or not.

block.description: The additional column for the Webhook Data Source table.

backfill.description: Whether historical data should be backfilled or not.

destination.description: The Materialized View's destination (AKA "target") Data Pool.

environment.description: The Environment that the Materialized View belongs to.

others.description: Other Data Pools queried by the Materialized View.

source.description: The Materialized View's source Data Pool.

sql.description: The SQL that the Materialized View executes.

id.description: The ID of the Data Pool.

block.description: If specified, the Materialized View will target an existing Data Pool. Ensure the Data Pool's schema is compatible with your Materialized View's SQL statement.

access_control_enabled.description: Enables or disables access control for the Data Pool. If the Data Pool has access control enabled, Applications must be assigned Data Pool Access Policies in order to query the Data Pool and its Metrics.

timestamp.description: Optionally specify the Data Pool's primary timestamp. This will influence the Data Pool's engine settings.

order_by.description: The ORDER BY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

partition_by.description: The PARTITION BY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

primary_key.description: The PRIMARY KEY clause for the Data Pool's table. This field is optional. A default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if specified.

columns.description: The columns argument for the SummingMergeTree table engine.

ver.description: The `ver` parameter to the ReplacingMergeTree table engine.

Override the Data Pool's table settings. These describe how the Data Pool's table is created in ClickHouse, and a default will be chosen based on the Data Pool's `timestamp` and `uniqueId` values, if any. You can override these defaults in order to specify a custom table engine, custom ORDER BY, etc.
If specified, the Materialized View will create and target a new Data Pool. You can further customize the new Data Pool's engine settings.
Provides a Propel Materialized View resource. This can be used to create and manage Propel Materialized Views.

access_control_enabled.description: Whether or not access control is enabled for the Metric.

data_pool.description: The Data Pool that powers this Metric.

dimension.description: The Dimension where the count distinct operation is going to be performed. Only valid for COUNT_DISTINCT Metrics.

dimensions.description: The Metric's Dimensions. These Dimensions are available to Query Filters.

expression.description: The custom expression for aggregating data in a Metric. Only valid for CUSTOM Metrics.

measure.description: The Dimension to be summed, taken the minimum of, taken the maximum of, averaged, etc. Only valid for SUM, MIN, MAX and AVERAGE Metrics.

type.description: The Metric type. The different Metric types determine how the values are calculated.

and.description: Additional filters to AND with this one. AND takes precedence over OR. It is defined as a JSON string value.

column.description: The name of the column to filter on.

operator.description: The operation to perform when comparing the column and filter values.

or.description: Additional filters to OR with this one. AND takes precedence over OR. It is defined as a JSON string value.

value.description: The value to compare the column to.

block.description: Metric Filters allow defining a Metric with a subset of records from the given Data Pool. If no Metric Filters are present, all records will be included. To filter at query time, add Dimensions and use the `filters` property on the `timeSeriesInput`, `counterInput`, or `leaderboardInput` objects. There is no need to add `filters` to be able to filter at query time.
Provides a Propel Metric resource. This can be used to create and manage Propel Metrics.

application.description: The Application that is granted access.

metric.description: The Metric that the Application is granted access to.

type.description: The Policy type. The different Policy types determine the access to the Metric data.

block.description: Provides a Propel Policy resource. This can be used to create and manage Propel Access Policies. It governs an Application's access to a Metric's data.
